alternatives.text: WITHIN THE RANGE, the 45 m2 model offers 12 m2 more but sits EXACTLY on the Class 3A ceiling with no tolerance, and the 48 m2 model is over it — so this is the safe end of the range and the step up carries real regulatory risk. ELSEWHERE, All About Outdoors' habitable units and Rayco Modular Homes face the same 32–45 m2 arithmetic; ÖÖD House's glass units are habitable-use products with the same exclusion from the incidental exemption. IF THE REQUIREMENT IS DAY SPACE ONLY, an exempt garden room is far simpler. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within Class 3A, choose the size with margin rather than the size at the limit.

THE 33 m2 MODEL IS THE RISK-AVERSE ALTERNATIVE: 12 m2 smaller, but with 12 m2 of margin inside the band rather than none. THE 48 m2 MODEL IS THE OPPOSITE TRADE — 3 m2 more space at the cost of leaving Class 3A entirely and requiring a full application. ELSEWHERE IN THE CATALOGUE, Rayco Modular Homes and All About Outdoors market habitable units in the same size territory and face identical arithmetic; Yardbox's Bothan is the record whose published living space exceeds its own stated footprint, and is not a safe comparator on area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 45 m2 the choice is between maximum space and margin for error — there is no option that offers both.

THE 45 m2 MODEL IS THE OBVIOUS COMPARISON AND FOR MOST HOUSEHOLDS THE BETTER ONE: 3 m2 smaller, but inside Class 3A and therefore a notice rather than an application. ELSEWHERE, Rayco Modular Homes and All About Outdoors market habitable units of similar scale and face the same threshold; ÖÖD House's glass units are habitable-use products excluded from the incidental exemption on the same principle. SUPPLIER STATUS — GRANNY FLATS DUBLIN, 4 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All four are HABITABLE DWELLINGS and therefore excluded from the 30 m2 incidental garden-structure exemption at any size, which permits no human habitation. Against the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling provision of S.I. 338 of 2026 the four fall into three distinct positions: the Studio at 25.00 m2 is BELOW the 32 m2 floor; the 1 Bed at 33.00 m2 and the 1 or 2 Bed at 45.00 m2 are WITHIN the 32–45 m2 band, the latter EXACTLY on the ceiling with zero tolerance; and the 2 Bed at 48.00 m2 EXCEEDS it. Every floor area is published in the product name and verified. THE CATALOGUE LIMITATION APPLYING TO ALL FOUR: no height, U-value, warranty, price, room dimensions or measurement basis is published, so the products are distinguished on area and bedroom count alone and evidence neutrality is preserved on build quality. Nothing inferred.

THE WELLNESS COHORT IN THIS CATALOGUE IS SMALL AND UNIFORMLY UNDOCUMENTED ON SIZE. TimberIN offers four products — a wood-fired hot tub, a cold plunge tub, a made-to-order barrel sauna and a sauna-and-hot-tub combo — of which only the enclosed ones are structures for planning purposes. MyCabin.ie's Cube Sauna M is the Irish-supplier alternative. None publishes a footprint. THE MORE USEFUL COMPARISON MAY BE OUTSIDE THE CATEGORY: if the sauna is intended to share a garden with a future office, look at what the office will need — Adman's nine named Multiroom sizes from 9.60 m2 upward, or Yardbox's published footprints — and reserve the allowance now. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: plan the whole garden, not the next purchase. SUPPLIER STATUS — AUROOM WELLNESS, 2 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Neither the Quu nor the Aurea publishes an area, footprint, height, specification, warranty or price, and Atlas records no distinguishing evidence between the two models — recorded once as a catalogue limitation. CATEGORY ISSUE carried forward once: both are wellness and sauna cabins held under Garden Rooms because no correct Product Category exists, and they should not be compared like-for-like against work-use garden rooms. Nothing inferred.

WITHIN THE WELLNESS GROUP IN THIS CATALOGUE, the comparisons are TimberIN's Nordic Pod Custom barrel sauna — made to order, so the size is set by the commission — and its Nordic Hobbiton sauna-and-hot-tub combo, where the whole unit occupies one continuous footprint. MyCabin.ie's Cube Sauna M is the Irish-supplier option, though the 'M' is a size band rather than a measurement. All of them share the same gap: none publishes a footprint, so none can be tested against the allowance. IF THE REAL REQUIREMENT IS A WARM YEAR-ROUND ROOM RATHER THAN A SAUNA, the certified thermal work points elsewhere entirely — SIPS-House publishes 124 mm SIPS walls and a 0.031 W/mK core, and Sanctum and Yardbox publish usable internal area separately from footprint. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: decide first whether you are buying heat or space; they are different products.

IF THE APPEAL IS AN IRISH SHED-AND-GARDEN-BUILDING MAKER, Atlas holds several with real published figures. MCD Garden Sheds offers four models by roof type and configuration — though it too publishes no dimensions. Adman Steel Sheds is the better documented comparison: nine Multiroom sizes from 9.60 m2 to 36.80 m2, every one named by an explicit two-dimension designation, so the planning test can actually be run before you order. Shanette Sheds publishes two Gold Range sizes, one inside the allowance at 24.80 m2 and one over it at 31.20 m2. MyCabin.ie is Irish with three showrooms and publishes dimensions for every model. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: prefer a supplier whose sizes you can check on a page rather than one you must telephone to discover. SUPPLIER STATUS — BALLYFREE GARDEN SHEDS, 1 Garden Room product, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). The single Atlas record names a product type rather than a model and carries no area, dimension, height, specification or price, so all five Decision Intelligence values record an evidenced absence. INTEGRITY NOTE recorded once: this record should be split into the supplier's actual models before it is surfaced to homeowners; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. Nothing inferred.

THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL COMPARISON FOR A CROSS-BORDER BUYER IS YARDBOX, which serves BOTH Irish jurisdictions and publishes footprint, usable living space and a 2.5 m height per model — removing at once the two questions this range leaves open. For a sculptural form with more published detail, Iglucraft and Koto are the nearest records. SUPPLIER STATUS — BERKO POD SYSTEMS, 3 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). The Beehive, The Shepherds Hut and The Luxury Lodge carry no verified floor area, dimension, height, warranty or price, so no product could be distinguished from another on any measured basis and EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED ON SPECIFICATION throughout. THE THREE ARE DIFFERENTIATED HERE ONLY BY WHAT THE CERTIFIED LAYERS ESTABLISH — the habitable-use designations on the Lodge and the Hut, and their absence on the Beehive. TWO OBSTACLES GOVERN THE WHOLE RANGE, as already recorded in the certified Planning layer, and neither is about size: JURISDICTION, since Berko operates from Northern Ireland where the Irish exempted-development regime does not apply, so supplier guidance must not be read across to a Republic site; and USE, since overnight occupation removes the Class 3 exemption at any floor area, leaving the Class 3A route (32–45 m2, rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) untestable without an area. BOUNDARY NOTE, carried from the certified layer: Berko's fourth product, The Treehouse, sits in the Treehouses category outside the Garden Room boundary and is counted separately. Nothing inferred.

FOR OVERNIGHT ACCOMMODATION ON A REPUBLIC SITE WITH A PUBLISHED AREA AND A CLEAR ROUTE, Granny Flats Dublin's 1 Bed at 33.00 m2 and 1 or 2 Bed at 45.00 m2 are built around the Class 3A band and state their floor areas — the decisive difference from this record. FOR A GLAMPING OR LETTING VENTURE, ÖÖD's Glämping House is the catalogue's other openly hospitality-oriented product, equally undimensioned. FOR AN EXEMPT DAY ROOM INSTEAD, Yardbox serves BOTH Irish jurisdictions with published footprints and heights — the one supplier here that removes the cross-border question entirely. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for habitable use, a published floor area is the qualifying test, not a detail.

FOR A SMALL DAY ROOM WITH THE FIGURES ALREADY PUBLISHED, Yardbox's Whistler gives a 3.2 m × 3.2 m footprint, 9 m2 of living space and a 2.5 m height, and serves BOTH Irish jurisdictions — which also removes the cross-border question this record raises. Garden Solutions 4U's THE HOP at 8.92 m2 is the simpler Irish option. FOR OVERNIGHT USE, the Class 3A route and Granny Flats Dublin's dimensioned units are the correct comparison. WITHIN BERKO, the Beehive is the other compact form. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the hut will be slept in, compare it with dwellings, not with garden rooms.

FOR THE SAME SIZE-TO-FIT ADVANTAGE WITH MORE BEHIND IT, Modular Outlook Ireland is made-to-order and at least names its construction system — SIP panel — which this record does not. Modular Innovations publishes a 10-30 m2 band, giving much of the same flexibility while telling a buyer the limits in advance. Essex Garden Studios is bespoke but serves South East England only. IF A FIXED PRODUCT WOULD ACTUALLY DO, the catalogue offers far better evidence: Adman Steel Sheds publishes nine named Multiroom sizes from 9.60 to 36.80 m2, so a buyer can usually find a standard size that fits the remaining allowance without commissioning anything, and Yardbox publishes footprint, usable area and height for all three models. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bespoke is worth paying for when the plot demands it — not when a catalogue size would have fitted.

WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES: the Multi Use Home Office is the same construction as an undivided shell; the Home Office with Storage commits part of the footprint to a store; the Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette adds plumbing and a harder consent question. OUTSIDE: Cabin Master names PHOTOGRAPHY STUDIOS as a stated use case and builds on site with no crane constraint, though it publishes no Irish route; Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included, no crane and no concrete foundation — the direct answer if access is the obstacle; Garden Office Solutions fits TRIPLE GLAZING as standard and includes electrics, painting and foundations in a delivered price, on a Kildare-centred regional footprint. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes. SUPPLIER STATUS — BIG MAN TINY HOMES, 4 Garden-Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All 4 now carry the full five-Feature AM-007 set: Home Office w/ Storage, Home Office w/ Bathroom & Kitchenette, Multi Use Home Office and Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL SYNTHESIS, and it is unusual enough to be diagnostic: THIS SUPPLIER SELLS CONFIGURATIONS, NOT SIZES. Not one of the four model names carries a dimension — every name describes FIT-OUT or USE instead. Atlas has created no ranking between the four, because all share one construction system and none carries an area. THREE GENUINE STRENGTHS, each a catalogue first or near-first. ONE, THE CONSTRUCTION PAIRING: SIPS structural insulated panels from a named European manufacturer WITH EcoTherm rigid PIR in all walls, roof and ceiling — the certified thermal layer records that this combines the two strongest construction ideas found separately elsewhere in the Atlas and that NO OTHER SUPPLIER MATCHES IT; Loghouse builds in SIPS but on a lower-performing EPS core. TWO, ENGINEER CERTIFICATION BEFORE DISPATCH: each unit is built in full at the Bandon premises and signed off by the supplier's own engineer before it leaves. No other supplier in this catalogue publishes that step, and it moves the quality risk off the site entirely. THREE, A PUBLISHED 20-YEAR GUARANTEE — the second-longest defined term in the Atlas behind only Garden Office Solutions at fifty, and materially more defensible written over a factory-built, engineer-certified object. FOUR LIMITATIONS, each restated once and not re-raised. ONE, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED FOR ANY PRODUCT — no floor areas, no dimensions, no heights — so the planning area test cannot be run anywhere in this range and none is rankable on any basis. TWO, THE FIT-OUT IS THE PLANNING ISSUE ON TWO OF THE FOUR: the bathroom-and-kitchenette unit is equipped for habitation and would fall outside Class 3 ON USE whatever its area, and the treatment room raises change of use — so obtaining the areas would resolve only half this range. THREE, THE WARRANTY IS LENGTH WITHOUT DETAIL: no scope, exclusions, claims procedure or transferability published, and no confirmation the term reaches the home-office configurations rather than only the residential tiny homes the phrase names. FOUR, THERMAL QUANTIFICATION: no SIPS panel thickness and no U-value published, and the 'A BER rating' claim rates whole DWELLINGS on energy use rather than garden buildings on fabric. AVAILABILITY: AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND — an Irish manufacturer at Clancool Beg, Bandon, Co. Cork, P72 H763, with over twenty years' building experience; a sister operation, Big Man Modular, trades from the same address and is retained as a distinct organisation. NO DELIVERY RADIUS IS PUBLISHED, and because units are built complete and CRANED onto site, the practical limit is haulage and lift access rather than trade area — crane access is the gating physical constraint and the BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED across the range. Press-reported context, recorded as such: six-to-eight-week build; a 25 m2 bathroom-and-kitchenette unit at EUR 60,000-70,000. No new outstanding integrity issues arise from this supplier.

WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES, AND THIS IS THE COMPARISON THAT MATTERS: the Multi Use Home Office, the Home Office with Storage and the Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room share the identical construction but WITHOUT the bathroom and kitchenette — which means they stand a chance under the incidental-use exemption that this configuration is unlikely to meet. If you do not need to sleep or cook in the building, one of those three is the simpler consent route. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, for a buyer who does want self-contained accommodation: Luxury Garden Studios delivers heated, fitted units with a kitchen and full bathroom at one price with no staged extras, on a 10-year structural warranty — though Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed from its Northern Ireland base. Concept Modular publishes a 50-year structural warranty on steel-framed buildings with a designer kitchen and bathroom, excluding base pads, installation, craneage and haulage at EUR 3,000-4,000 plus VAT. Sprout Pod needs no crane and no concrete foundation, if access is the obstacle. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; every one of them raises the same habitation question.

WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES: the Multi Use Home Office is the same construction without the fixed storage division; the Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room is the higher-specification configuration; the Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette adds plumbing and, with it, a materially harder planning question. The certified layers record that this supplier SELLS CONFIGURATIONS, NOT SIZES — not one model name carries a dimension — so Atlas creates no ranking between the four and the choice is fit-out. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) publishes a directly comparable ROOM-PLUS-STORE COMBO in one envelope, at a stated 18 m2 nominal, which is the nearest equivalent proposition in the catalogue with a number attached — though its coverage is Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford only. Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included, NO CRANE and no concrete foundation — the direct answer if crane access is the obstacle here. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, the only route on which this supplier's unquantified SIPS envelope can be benchmarked. Cabin Master builds on site with no access constraint at all. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, access and scope, not on measured performance.

WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES: the Home Office with Storage commits part of the footprint to a store; the Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room is the higher-specification configuration; the Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette adds plumbing and a materially harder planning question. All four share one construction system, and the certified layers record that this supplier sells CONFIGURATIONS, NOT SIZES — no model name carries a dimension — so Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included, NO CRANE and no concrete foundation — the direct answer if crane access is the obstacle, and the closest comparable turnkey position. Loghouse also builds in SIPS, on an EPS core rather than PIR, and publishes coverage across all 32 counties, so it is the nearest system-comparable route with a wider footprint. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, the only route on which this supplier's unquantified SIPS envelope can be benchmarked numerically. Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue — the direct remedy where no area is published at all. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, access and coverage, not on measured performance.

ANY OF THE NINE MEASURED LASITA MODELS IS A BETTER STARTING POINT THAN A PAGE THAT RETURNS NOTHING — and for a workspace specifically, the NEW YORK at 20.40 m2 external is the only one the manufacturer lists for workshop and office use. FOR A CLEAN COMPARISON WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Loghouse, Adman, MyCabin.ie and Timber Living all publish sizes and deliver in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: when a catalogue entry cannot be verified as a current product, start again with one that can. ——— SUPPLIER STATUS: LASITA MAJA — 10 Garden Room products — DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. THE HEADLINE FINDING IS CATEGORY, AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OF ANY SUPPLIER IN THIS LAYER: OF THE TEN PRODUCTS ATLAS HOLDS AS GARDEN ROOMS, THE MANUFACTURER LISTS ONLY THE NEW YORK FOR 'WORKSHOP & OFFICE' USE. The FALKLAND and HAWAII are GARAGES sold for vehicles, with wooden or Hormann garage doors. The SACRAMENTO, MIAMI 2.0, CARROZ and NEW ORLEANS are listed for 'Storage' only. The DOMEO 10 and ORINOCO are outdoor-living models. NINE OF TEN ARE THEREFORE MISCATEGORISED for a homeowner searching for a workspace, and wall profiles of 28–34 mm on several confirm they are not year-round buildings. Category debt carried forward, recorded and not corrected. ON MEASUREMENT LASITA IS THE BEST DISCLOSER IN THE CATALOGUE: nine of ten carry a VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA and are SAFE TO RANK on usable floor — Sacramento 8.2, Miami 2.0 8.2, Orinoco 14.9, Carroz 15.96, Domeo 10 19.01, New York 19.74, New Orleans 22.85, Falkland 32.06, Hawaii 39.42 m2 — because the manufacturer publishes 'Wall dimensions' as EXTERNAL and 'Floor size' as INTERNAL, the difference being exactly twice the wall thickness on each axis, reconciled to the centimetre on four separate products. Only the Brava is outstanding. ON PLANNING, FOUR OF THE NINE EXCEED the 30 m2 combined allowance on their external envelope — Falkland 33.06, Hawaii 40.56, Orinoco 37.50 and Domeo 10 38.25 m2 — and on the last two the internal floor is barely half the envelope, so the internal figure alone would badly mislead the exemption test. THE FALKLAND AND HAWAII ALSO BREACH THE 3 m HEIGHT LIMIT applying to their shingled roofs, and a SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT on the Orinoco (wall height 306 cm against ridge height 244.8 cm) makes its height position unresolvable from published evidence. THERMALLY ALL TEN ARE UNINSULATED, Tier B. Lasita offers the widest wall-thickness ladder in the Atlas — 19, 21, 28, 34, 40, 44, 70 and 92 mm — and the 92 mm is the thickest solid timber wall in this catalogue. BUT THICKNESS IS NOT INSULATION, AND THE DECISIVE DETAIL IS WHAT THE OPTIONAL KIT COVERS: Lasita's 'Complete Insulation Kit' insulates the FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY. THERE IS NO WALL INSULATION OPTION AT ALL, which distinguishes Lasita from Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde, each of which sells a wall package — so NO LASITA BUILDING CAN BE BROUGHT TO A FULLY INSULATED ENVELOPE THROUGH THE SUPPLIER'S OWN CATALOGUE, and a Lasita garden room remains a three-season building however much is spent on options. COMMERCIALLY: an ESTONIAN MANUFACTURER selling through independent retailers; INSTALLATION IS DIY KIT ONLY with free kit delivery, no assembly service, and the FOUNDATION THE BUYER'S RESPONSIBILITY — the manufacturer does not build, does not arrange a builder and does not provide the base; REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED with free delivery explicitly EXCLUDING Northern Ireland; and a WARRANTY of 2 or 5 years varying by model, with the term for individual models unpublished. TWO FURTHER FINDINGS CARRIED, NOT RE-RAISED: the MIAMI 2.0 and SACRAMENTO are published with identical specifications on every measured field except pallet weight and are the same building under two names; and a 'Carroz 2' and two further Hawaii listings create variant ambiguity. NOTHING WAS ESTIMATED AND NO RANKING WAS CREATED WHERE THE EVIDENCE CANNOT DISTINGUISH. NO NEW OUTSTANDING INTEGRITY ISSUE RAISED.

THE RAMSAY 70 A ALU AT 22.62 m2 AND THE DUBLIN 70 AT 22.15 m2 ARE THE LARGER MODELS IN THE RANGE, both flat-roofed and both also uninsulated. FOR A ROOM THAT ARRIVES INSULATED AND ROOFED, Pineca's insulated builds publish U-values and Timber Living's Sunny carries a 93 mm insulated frame, both with Irish routes. FOR A COMPARABLE SIZE WITH A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Timber Living's Laura at 4.0 × 4.0 m states an eaves height and pitch. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: add the roof covering and the insulation to this price before setting it beside any turnkey quotation.

WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the five named styles are the same construction with a use attached; if your requirement matches one, start there. OUTSIDE: My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) is the closest Irish on-site builder publishing sizes and a two-tier price structure, covering Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford; Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation; Modern Garden Rooms holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas with foundations inside scope; Pineca Ireland is the only supplier publishing U-values. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 now carry the full five-Feature AM-007 set: Extra Living Space, Home Office, Home Gym, Salon / Studio, Sensory Room and Bespoke Build. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL SYNTHESIS: this is a BESPOKE ON-SITE BUILDER, not a catalogue supplier. CG Joinery Ltd is family-run, established 2009, working from a garden-room showroom at 7 Ryan Rd, Mayobridge, Newry, BT34 2HZ. Its published range is SIX USE STYLES, not six models — there are no sizes, no dimensions and no prices anywhere on the site — so all six share one construction system, one installation model, one availability position and one contested warranty position, and Atlas has created NO RANKING between them. The choice is intended use, nothing more. FOUR GENUINE STRENGTHS AGAINST THE CATALOGUE. ONE, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED: built on site from start to finish, which removes the constraint that eliminates Big Man Tiny Homes, ÖÖD and other craned-unit suppliers on tight plots. TWO, THE STRONGEST CROSS-BORDER EVIDENCE OF ANY NORTHERN IRELAND SUPPLIER IN THIS ATLAS — a dedicated ROI phone line, dedicated Dublin, Dundalk, Drogheda and Swords location pages, and euro pricing; where Luxury Garden Studios is recorded REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED on an Ireland-facing page alone, this supplier publishes commitments. THREE, A FULLY PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE — 10 / 50 / 40 per cent with finance available — which very few suppliers in this catalogue publish at all. FOUR, IT PUBLISHES NO INCORRECT IRISH PLANNING CLAIM, declining to state a threshold and directing buyers to check local regulations; that is the correct position for a cross-border supplier and rarer in this catalogue than it should be. THE DECISIVE LIMITATION, RECORDED ONCE AND FLAGGED FOR CHANGE CONTROL: THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED. A '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' are both published on the same page, the shorter figure repeated in the supplier's own FAQ. Ten years would place CG Garden Rooms at the Irish market norm; ten months would place it below every published term in this Atlas. Atlas records both and resolves neither. THREE FURTHER LIMITATIONS, each recorded once: no area, dimensions or prices published for any product, so nothing in this range is rankable; no insulation material, thickness or U-value published, so the envelope is established as insulated but not quantifiable; and the base position is unpublished, alongside an internal inconsistency between 'built on site from start to finish' and separately marketed 'modular garden rooms' made in sections. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: a credible, accessible, genuinely cross-border on-site builder whose entire specification is created at the design meeting. Arrive prepared, and get the drawing, the build-up, the base position and the warranty term in writing before the deposit.

WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: all six styles share one construction system, one installation model and one contested warranty position, so the choice is fit-out and intended use rather than performance — Atlas creates no ranking between them. If the room is genuinely multi-purpose, the Bespoke Build is the same proposition without a use label attached. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) is the closest comparable Irish on-site builder — it publishes NOMINAL SIZES for every model and a transparent two-tier price structure, so it is where to go if you want a number before you make contact, though its coverage is Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford only. Sprout Pod publishes island-wide free delivery and installation with heating included and no concrete foundation — the widest Irish coverage in the catalogue. Modern Garden Rooms, at a Dublin address, holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with foundations inside its turnkey scope — the direct answer if the unquantified envelope here concerns you. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ in what they publish and where they deliver, not in measured performance.

WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the identical construction without a use label, and would be the route if the room is to serve as gym and something else. All six styles share one system; Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, AND THIS IS THE COMPARISON A GYM BUYER SHOULD ACTUALLY MAKE: Booths Garden Studios is the only supplier in this Atlas publishing gym-specific engineering — a DECOUPLED FLOOR built to accommodate movement, stated as helpful for treadmills and cross-trainers, and an EXTENDED INTERNAL HEIGHT OPTION of 7 ft 10 in described as popular with home gyms. It also names its insulation products and thicknesses. Its limitation is decisive here: NO IRISH DELIVERY IS PUBLISHED. Cabin Master builds three sized gyms on site with named insulation and foundations inside the price, but is also UK only. Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ in what they publish and where they deliver, not in measured performance.

WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the same construction without a use label, and the Extra Living Space is the same building specified for family use — all six styles share one system, so Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: Garden Office Solutions is the direct Irish comparison on specification — it fits TRIPLE GLAZING as standard, the only genuine triple-glazed standard in this Atlas, and publishes delivered prices with installation, electrics, painting and galvanised steel foundations inside the figure, though its coverage is a Kildare-centred regional footprint and its own 50-year headline attaches to the roof membrane rather than the building. My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) is the closest on-site builder that publishes sizes and a two-tier price structure, covering Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford. Sprout Pod delivers and installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, and the only route on which this supplier's unquantified envelope can be benchmarked. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ in published evidence and coverage, not measured performance.

WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the identical construction without a use label and would suit a practice needing an unusual layout; the Home Office is the same building where no clients visit, which is a materially simpler planning position. All six share one system; Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: Big Man Tiny Homes publishes a Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room, factory-built in SIPS with EcoTherm PIR and CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER before dispatch — the only engineer sign-off published in this Atlas, and directly relevant where a consistent client-facing finish is the commercial requirement; it needs crane access and is Cork-based. Its Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette is the route if plumbing is essential, though it carries a harder consent question. Garden Office Solutions fits triple glazing as standard with a delivered price including electrics and foundations, on a Kildare-centred footprint. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; each raises the same change-of-use question for a client-facing business.

THERE IS NO DIRECT ALTERNATIVE IN THIS ATLAS, and that is the honest answer: across 385 certified Garden Room products, no other supplier publishes a sensory room. WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the identical construction with the use undeclared, and would be the route if you would rather specify the acoustic and sensory requirements yourself from a blank sheet than accept a named style. THE NEAREST ADJACENT ROUTES, each answering part of the requirement rather than the whole: Oeco Garden Rooms publishes a SOUNDPROOF MUSIC ROOM — the only acoustically-specialised product in the catalogue, and the closest thing to an evidenced acoustic position, though it is a UK supplier. Big Man Tiny Homes builds in SIPS with EcoTherm PIR and certifies each unit with its own engineer before dispatch, which gives a controlled and consistent build — but needs crane access. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, if thermal stability is the priority. NEUTRALITY: none of these is a sensory room, and none is presented as equivalent; they are recorded as the nearest published capabilities.

IF THE APPEAL IS A CONTEMPORARY SQUARE-PLAN ROOM, the catalogue holds documented options. Yardbox's Whistler is a true 3.2 m square with a published 10.24 m2 footprint, 9 m2 living space and a 2.5 m height, from a supplier serving both Irish jurisdictions. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 3.2m at 9.60 m2 and 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 are near-square with explicit designations. Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m at 9.00 m2 is square and explicitly insulated. IF THE APPEAL IS THE SUPPLIER RATHER THAN THE FORM, this organisation's own Bespoke Garden Room at least lets the size be specified to the site, which a range name cannot. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: every one of these alternatives can be checked against your remaining allowance before you enquire; this record cannot.

TWO PRODUCTS TURN ON SOMETHING OTHER THAN AREA: the GUEST ROOM is excluded from Class 3 on HABITATION whatever its size, with Class 3A (32–45 m2) the only possible route and its 32 m2 floor meaning a smaller unit falls between both; and the GOLF SIMULATOR ROOM and GYM are constrained by INTERNAL CLEAR HEIGHT against a 3 m external cap, neither figure published. NO U-VALUE IS PUBLISHED FOR ANY ELEMENT OR ANY PRODUCT. NOTHING WAS ESTIMATED AND NO RANKING WAS CREATED WHERE THE EVIDENCE CANNOT DISTINGUISH. NO NEW OUTSTANDING INTEGRITY ISSUE RAISED.

Within the same supplier's range, Hansa Lounge XL publishes 14.5 m2 in a 592 x 502 cm envelope for EUR 8,700, and Hansa Lounge Mini publishes 9 m2 in 447 x 397 cm for EUR 7,320 — a three-step size ladder on one model family. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the three differ in published size and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

The Hansa Lounge family runs Mini at 9 m2 (447 x 397 cm, EUR 7,320), Lounge at 11.26 m2 (497 x 497 cm, EUR 8,100), this XL at 14.5 m2, and XXL variants at 22 to 24 m2 on 70 mm walls. Buyers needing to stay well inside the statutory allowance should compare Mini or Lounge. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the family differs in published size, wall thickness and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

WITHIN THIS RANGE THE MODULAR GARDEN ROOM SHARES THE 100 mm INSULATED STANDARD and the Golf Simulator Room uses SIP panels, so the range is not thermally uniform. FOR A PUBLISHED U-VALUE AND A TESTABLE AREA, Pineca's High-Quality Insulation Office states 0.156 W/(m2K) with a 15 m2 nominal size, and Timber Living's Sunny publishes four sizes with a 93 mm insulated frame and a 10-year guarantee from practical completion. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this specification is probably the best in the Atlas — but Pineca lets you prove it and this supplier does not.

THE MODERN GARDEN ROOM TRINITY AND THE CONTEMPORARY GARDEN ROOMS LEO AND AURORA ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THIS RECORD on published evidence. FOR A CONTEMPORARY ROOM WHERE THE FIGURES ARE ALREADY SETTLED, Yardbox publishes footprint, usable living space and a 2.5 m height per model across both Irish jurisdictions, and Outdoor Living's ModPod Vaya at 18.7 m2 and Nova at 22.5 m2 state real areas with an Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: when four models in one range cannot be told apart, the comparison worth making is with a supplier that publishes.

Atlas records this product as the representative of a two-row cluster sharing 9.7 m2, 21 mm and 657 x 288 cm: this model at EUR 7,250 and Garden House Leon at EUR 10,320. The smaller Elias publishes 7.3 m2 on 567 x 288 cm for EUR 6,530. Atlas also holds Contemporary Garden Room Leo at 9.7 m2 on 378 x 288 cm for EUR 8,570, which has no veranda. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: within the cluster the supplier publishes no specification difference, so no published evidence distinguishes the two on build.

The direct comparison is Elias XL, sharing the 288 cm depth and 21 mm wall at 657 cm long, publishing 9.7 m2 for EUR 7,250. Buyers wanting the same room without the veranda should compare Noah (7.3 m2, 288 x 288 cm, EUR 4,780). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the three differ in published length, room area and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

The direct comparison is Grace ALU, already in Atlas, on the identical 783 x 385 cm envelope at 19 m2 for EUR 9,480. Buyers needing to stay inside the statutory allowance should instead compare Ian A (18 m2, 70 mm, 478 x 388 cm, 18.55 m2 footprint, EUR 8,180) or Atlas-held Aurora (18 m2, 44 mm, 600 x 340 cm). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the published data does not establish any of these as the better build; they differ in footprint, wall thickness and price only.

Buyers wanting a 70 mm wall inside the statutory allowance should compare Garden Office Room Roland 1 (14 m2 room, 320 x 520 cm, 16.64 m2 footprint, EUR 13,610 — the same price) or Summer House Sommerland A (14 m2, 388 x 545 cm, 21.15 m2, EUR 11,030). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: all three publish a 70 mm wall and no insulation specification, so the published data cannot rank them on thermal performance.

THE MODERN GARDEN ROOM CLARA AND THE CONTEMPORARY GARDEN ROOMS LEO AND AURORA ARE THE PARALLEL RECORDS, none distinguishable from this one on published evidence; the Large Modern Garden Room Roberta is the size above. FOR A CONTEMPORARY ROOM WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Yardbox states footprint, living space and a 2.5 m height per model, and Outdoor Living's ModPod pods publish real areas at 18.7, 22.5 and 26.18 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a flat-roofed contemporary building, a published height is the figure that settles the exemption.

WITHIN THE RANGE, THE MODERN GARDEN GYM IS THE OTHER SPORTING-USE RECORD and carries the same unresolved internal-height question. OUTSIDE IT, Cabin Master publishes Garden Gyms at 4m × 3m, 5m × 3m and 6m × 3m with real dimensions, and Timber Living's Laura publishes an eaves height of approximately 2.08 m with a roughly 15-degree pitch — which is exactly the kind of figure a simulator buyer needs. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for any swing-clearance use, a supplier who publishes heights is worth more than one who publishes a panel system.

THE MODERN GARDEN OFFICE IN THE SAME RANGE CARRIES A HIGHER RECORDED WALL SPECIFICATION — 150 mm total against this record's 100 mm — so within one supplier the specification is not uniform and it is worth asking which applies. FOR A FINISHED ROOM WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Sprout Pod delivers built, wired and heated with free island-wide installation, and Timber Living builds on site in two visits with delivery and VAT included and a 10-year guarantee. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: several Irish suppliers now hand over a finished room — compare on what is published, not only on what is included.

Buyers wanting more integrated storage should compare Super Lucas E (15 m2 room, shed and veranda, 758 x 318 cm, EUR 9,050 at 44 mm) or Paula (12.5 m2 room plus store shed, EUR 9,170 at 44 mm). Buyers wanting the same 70 mm wall without a shed should compare Sommerland A (14 m2, EUR 11,030). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: these differ in published wall thickness, size and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

The direct comparison is Hansa Lounge XXL Pool Edition, on a near-identical 783 x 501 cm envelope but publishing 24 m2 at 70 mm for EUR 13,780 — more room and a thicker wall for EUR 1,030 more, though also outside the allowance. Buyers needing to stay inside it with integrated storage should compare Liam Plus (23.25 m2 footprint, 22 m2, EUR 10,420). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: no published evidence establishes any of these as the better build.

The Remo family spans three very different sizes: Remo 3 (6.5 m2 room, 58 mm, 553 x 398 cm, EUR 9,110), Remo 2 (8 m2, 58 mm, 408 x 498 cm, EUR 10,230) and this model at 22 m2 and 70 mm. Buyers wanting a large veranda inside the statutory allowance should compare Sommerland B (25.96 m2 footprint, EUR 11,890). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: these differ in published size, wall thickness and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

FOR THE SAME CHOOSE-YOUR-SIZE ADVANTAGE WITH MORE PUBLISHED DETAIL, Adman Steel Sheds is the strongest comparison in this catalogue: nine Multiroom sizes from 9.60 m2 to 36.80 m2, each named by an explicit two-dimension designation, so a buyer can pick a size AND check its footprint before ordering — the same flexibility, resolved into real products. Waltons publishes four insulated sizes from 9.00 to 24.00 m2 in the same band. IF A TRUE BESPOKE ROUTE IS WANTED, the 'Garden Rooms' Bespoke Garden Room and Modular Outlook Ireland's made-to-order SIP panel room both set the footprint per commission. IF THE UPPER END OF THE BAND IS THE ATTRACTION, look at what 30 m2 actually means: All About Outdoors' Ontario XL and KC Modular's 6x5m Pavilion both sit exactly on the limit with zero headroom, which is the position a 30 m2 commission would put you in. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: prefer a range that names its sizes over one that states a band. SUPPLIER STATUS — MODULAR INNOVATIONS, 1 Garden Room record, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). The record describes a 10-30 m2 size band rather than a building, and carries no specification, warranty, installation scope or price. Catalogue issue recorded once: it should be split into models before launch. Nothing inferred.

FOR SIP CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICALLY, SIPS-House is the direct comparison and publishes far more: 124 mm SIPS walls, 174 mm roof, EPS carbon-treated core at 0.031 W/mK, EPDM roof and PVC double glazing as standard across the range. Its weakness is the mirror image of this record's — excellent envelope disclosure, no published sizes at all, and it is a Vilnius-based self-assembly kit with no confirmed Irish installation route. FOR MADE-TO-ORDER SIZING FROM AN IRISH-FACING SUPPLIER, Modular Innovations states a 10-30 m2 band and the 'Garden Rooms' Bespoke Garden Room sets the footprint per commission. FOR A FIXED, FULLY DOCUMENTED PRODUCT INSTEAD, Yardbox publishes footprint, usable internal area and height for every model and serves both Irish jurisdictions. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you want SIPs AND a price you can compare, you will have to ask for both — no supplier in this catalogue publishes them together. SUPPLIER STATUS — MODULAR OUTLOOK IRELAND, 1 Garden Room product, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. The record names its construction system, which is more than most, but is made-to-order with no fixed area, no published U-values, no warranty term and no price. Nothing inferred.

THE CARIN 44 A AT 8.35 m2 INDOOR IS THE SAME SIZE CLASS IN A 44 mm PROFILE, and the MAYO GARDEN OFFICE BOX M at 8.2 m2 is the same area in a 70 mm build with double glazing — all three are uninsulated as supplied. FOR A SMALL ROOM THAT ARRIVES FINISHED AND HEATED, Sprout Pod's 3m pods include sockets, lights, heating and flooring with free island-wide installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within Gardenhouse24 at 8 m2 the choice is log thickness; between suppliers it is whether the room arrives usable.

AT 9–10 m2 THE TIMBER COMPARISONS ARE WELL DOCUMENTED: Yardbox's Whistler publishes a 3.2 m × 3.2 m footprint, 9 m2 of living space and a 2.5 m height across both Irish jurisdictions; Loghouse's 3.0 m × 3.0 m at 9 m2 and MyCabin.ie's Laois at 9.00 m2 are the other Irish options; Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m states an insulated build. THE CHOICE IS REALLY BETWEEN MATERIALS: steel for durability and low maintenance, timber for a warmer envelope and a softer appearance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size every option is inside the allowance, so decide on maintenance and insulation instead.

WALTONS' THORESBY PREMIUM INSULATED 4m x 3m AT 12.00 m2 IS THE TIMBER EQUIVALENT and is sold explicitly on its insulation grade — the direct comparison if the thermal question is what concerns you. LOGHOUSE'S 4.0 m × 3.0 m at 12 m2 is the Irish timber option, though its steel roofing caps it at the 3 m height limit. FOR A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Yardbox states 2.5 m. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 is the squarest of the smaller units and the better room if the garden can take the depth. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size the material choice matters more than the four square metres.

WITHIN ADMAN, THE 4m x 4.2m AT 16.80 m2 IS THE BETTER ROOM for almost the same area, if the garden can take a 4 m depth — the single most useful comparison for this record. LOGHOUSE'S 5.0 m × 3.0 m at 15 m2 and Waltons' Thoresby Premium Insulated 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2 are the timber equivalents at the same proportion. FOR A PUBLISHED HEIGHT AND USABLE INTERNAL AREA, Yardbox states both across its range. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: where two models cost similar square metres of your allowance, the deeper one is usually the better building.

LOGHOUSE'S 6.0 m × 3.0 m AT 18 m2 IS THE DIRECT TIMBER EQUIVALENT at effectively the same size and proportion, from another Irish supplier, and it publishes external dimensions too. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 offers a metre more depth for two more square metres of allowance — usually the better trade if the garden width allows. FOR A DOCUMENTED HEIGHT, Yardbox states 2.5 m. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 11 m2 of remaining allowance, the choice between this and the deeper model should be made after measuring what is already in the garden, not before.

THE ONLY OTHER PRODUCTS IN THE CATALOGUE THIS CLOSE TO THE LIMIT ARE ALL ABOUT OUTDOORS' ONTARIO XL AT 30 m2 AND KC MODULAR'S 6x5m PAVILION AT 30.00 m2 — both at exactly the line with zero headroom and, in the Ontario XL's case, an unstated measurement basis. NONE OF THE THREE IS SAFE ON AN OCCUPIED GARDEN. FOR A COMPARABLE AREA WITH BETTER PROPORTION AND A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Yardbox's Vancouver at 24.00 m2 gives up 3.60 m2 and returns depth, documentation and margin. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 is the sensible retreat. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: near the threshold, margin is worth more than area.

SIPS Garden Room ALOE — 20.8m² from EUR 9,990 ex VAT: a far stronger thermal envelope (SIPS at 0.031 W/mK versus 40mm) for less money, but as a self-assembly kit rather than a finished unit. Duraboard Garden Room Mid Size 4.5m x 3m (My Garden Room) — EUR 19,600 estimated full turnkey with base, electrics and finishes included. Concept Modular Standard Office — EUR 16,950 ex VAT with a 50-year structural warranty if longevity is the priority.

LOGHOUSE'S 5.0 m × 4.0 m AT 20 m2 IS THE TIMBER EQUIVALENT at effectively the same size and proportion, also Irish and also publishing external dimensions. YARDBOX'S VANCOUVER AT 24.00 m2 goes larger and publishes usable living space and a 2.5 m height as well as a footprint — the most complete documentation available at this scale. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 restores a comfortable margin for four square metres less, and the 4m x 6.2m at 24.80 m2 reduces it to about 5 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the largest Adman model that leaves room for an ordinary shed.

YARDBOX'S VANCOUVER AT A PUBLISHED 24.00 m2 IS THE ANSWER TO THIS RECORD'S WEAKNESS: effectively the same size, but with usable living space and a 2.5 m height published alongside the footprint, so a buyer near the limit has figures to rely on. WALTONS' CLASSIC 6m x 4m at 24.00 m2 and Loghouse's 6.0 m × 4.0 m at 24 m2 are the timber equivalents, both also close to the limit. IF THE GARDEN HOLDS ANYTHING ELSE, the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 restores a workable margin. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: near the threshold, choose the supplier who publishes a measured figure.

TO STAY EXEMPT, THE 4m x 6.2m AT 24.80 m2 IS THE LARGEST ADMAN MODEL THAT QUALIFIES, and the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 the largest that leaves a workable margin. IF THE INTENTION IS HABITABLE ACCOMMODATION, Granny Flats Dublin's units are built around the Class 3A band and publish their areas. SUPPLIER STATUS — ADMAN STEEL SHEDS, 9 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All nine are Multiroom units named by an explicit two-dimension designation, so every one carries a usable nominal area and none required a verification classification — which makes Adman one of the better-documented suppliers in the catalogue on size and allows genuine evidence-based differentiation across the range. THE SPREAD IS THE OUTPUT: SEVEN sit inside the 30 m2 allowance on area (9.60, 12.60, 15.60, 16.80, 18.60, 20.80 and 24.80 m2), the 3m x 9.2m at 27.60 m2 is exempt ONLY because of the 27 July 2026 increase, and this 4m x 9.2m at 36.80 m2 exceeds the allowance outright. THE STANDING CAVEAT, carried from the certified layers: all nine figures are NOMINAL designations, not measured external footprints — Adman publishes no internal area and no conversion rule, and as STEEL buildings the wall build-up and internal loss differ from the timber ranges these would otherwise be compared against, so the two marginal units at 24.80 and 27.60 m2 should not be relied on without a dimensioned plan. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED ON ENVELOPE: no height, U-value, insulation specification, warranty or price exists for any model, so nothing has been ranked on build quality or thermal performance. Adman is an Irish manufacturer, so every position is directly actionable. Nothing inferred.

AT ROUGHLY 10 m2 WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Yardbox's Whistler is the better-documented equivalent: a 3.2 m x 3.2 m published footprint of 10.24 m2, 9 m2 of separately published living space, a 2.5 m height, from a Co. Down supplier serving Ireland and Northern Ireland — the same size, more disclosure, and obtainable. Elevate Modular's Ember publishes 4.27 m x 2.44 m with a dual-currency starting price. Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m at 9.00 m2 is explicitly insulated. Garden Solutions 4U's THE HOP 12ft x 8ft at about 8.92 m2 is the simpler, cheaper end of the band. IF THE MODULAR APPROACH IS THE ATTRACTION, the NOOK Double at 19.5 m2 is the same unit twice over. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the deciding factor at this size is not the area — several products match it — but whether the supplier will install in your garden.

AT AROUND 19 m2 WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, several records do what this one cannot. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 6.2m at 18.60 m2 and 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 bracket it with explicit two-dimension designations. Home Modular publishes 18 m2 from an Irish domain. Yardbox's Vancouver at a 16.64 m2 published footprint with 15 m2 living space and a 2.5 m height is the disclosure benchmark and serves both Irish jurisdictions. Green Retreats' G2 4.3m x 4.2m at 18.06 m2 is dimensionally close but delivers free only within 100 miles of Buckinghamshire. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size the catalogue is competitive, so availability and disclosure — not area — should decide it. SUPPLIER STATUS — NOOK PREFAB (ESPACIO NOOK), 2 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. Both records carry a published area in the product name, at 9.75 m2 and exactly double that at 19.5 m2, which is better size disclosure than most of this catalogue offers; neither states whether the figure is internal or external, and the exact 2:1 relationship shows the range is modular rather than separately measured. No construction specification, insulation value, height, warranty or price is held for either. Spanish-produced and sold via an online configurator with no published Irish installation route — the single fact most likely to decide whether either product is a real option. Nothing inferred.

THE NEW YORK IS THE ONLY LASITA MODEL LISTED FOR WORKSHOP AND OFFICE USE and is the record to move to if a workspace is what is wanted. FOR STORAGE AT SCALE WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Adman's steel and timber range and My Garden Room's room-and-store combos publish areas and deliver in Ireland. FOR A WORKSPACE AT A SIMILAR AREA, Timber Living's Nila at 17.5 m2 or Loghouse's 24.44 m2 unit are honest comparisons. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a large building sold for storage is not a bargain garden office — it is a large shed.

WITHIN LASITA MAJA THERE IS NO SECOND WORKSPACE MODEL — the manufacturer lists the other nine for storage, outdoor living, holiday use or vehicles, so this record has no internal equivalent. FOR A COMPARABLE SIZE WITH AN IRISH ROUTE AND AN INSTALLED PRICE, Loghouse's 4.0 × 5.0 m at 20 m2 and Timber Living's Sunny at 21.02 m2 with a 93 mm insulated frame are the honest comparisons, and MyCabin.ie can be visited in three counties. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: Lasita gives the best numbers in the catalogue and the least service — decide which you need more.

THE LAURA AT 25 m2 IS THE NEAREST SIZE IN THE RANGE WITH FLOOR AND ROOF INSULATION OFFERED, and the SUNNY at 21.02 m2 is the only Timber Living model with an insulated WALL system — between them they cover the trade-off between size and warmth. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Garden Office Solutions publishes 25 and 26.4 m2 models and Outdoor Living's ModPod reaches 26.18 m2, both with Irish routes and insulated construction. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 27 m2 uninsulated, the honest comparison is against a smaller insulated room — not against a larger one.

THE OAK INSULATED 6 × 3 m IS THE SAME ENVELOPE AND THE SAME PLANNING POSITION, BUILT FOR WINTER — and at Pineca that is a decision made once. THE LAYLA INSULATED 6 × 3 m publishes a 15 m2 internal floor for the same external size, which shows what the insulated build actually costs in space. FOR AN UNINSULATED LOG ROOM WITH A LATER UPGRADE PATH, Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde all sell separate wall-insulation packages; Loghouse publishes eight sizes with an Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if there is any chance you will want winter use, the retrofit rule makes the insulated version the safer buy.

THE HIGH-QUALITY INSULATION OFFICE IS THE ONE PINECA RECORD WITH PUBLISHED U-VALUES and is the tier to choose for permanent daily use; the LAYLA Insulated range covers 4 × 3, 5 × 3 and 6 × 3 m with published internal areas of 10, 13 and 15 m2. THE OAK 44 mm IS THE SAME ENVELOPE UNINSULATED and is a summer building, not a cheaper version of this one. OUTSIDE PINECA, Timber Living's Sunny and Outdoor Living's ModPod range are insulated with Irish installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within this supplier, the LAYLA models are the ones that publish an internal floor — which is what you actually get.

FOR ACOUSTIC ISOLATION SPECIFICALLY, the only other purpose-built option in this Atlas is SONIC BOX STUDIOS — four models, SB-1 Entry through SB-4 Pro, also room-within-a-room construction. It is a weaker record than this one in every documentary respect: no areas, no dimensions and no heights are published for any of the four, the model names denote acoustic tiers rather than sizes, and it is Sussex-based with no published Irish route either. FOR A MUSIC OR CINEMA ROOM FROM AN IRISH SUPPLIER, Shomera's For Life studios are sold by use — cinema, spin and golf — and Shomera is an established Irish company, but it publishes no footprint or height for any of them, so nothing can be tested. THE HONEST POSITION: no supplier in this catalogue currently offers a documented, Irish-available, purpose-built soundproof garden room. A buyer with this requirement will be commissioning acoustic work from a general garden-room supplier and should ask for the acoustic performance in writing. SUPPLIER STATUS — OECO GARDEN ROOMS, 1 Garden Room product covering 42 published size variants, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. Unusually strong on published size and price, blocked on Irish availability, and carrying an English permitted-development claim that does not apply here — corrected once in the certified AM-006 layer and not repeated as a product claim.

FOR LOG CABINS WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Loghouse, Lugarde, Hansa24 and Gardenhouse24 Ireland are the better-documented records in this catalogue and cover the same traditional construction. WITHIN ALL ABOUT OUTDOORS, the Ontario XL is the only model with any published area — useful as a benchmark, though its basis is unstated. IF THE PRIORITY IS A CONFIRMED EXEMPTION rather than the cabin aesthetic, Yardbox and Adman Steel Sheds publish external footprints and heights that can be tested directly. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: in a category where wall thickness is the whole issue, prefer the supplier who tells you which side they measured from.

The Sweden family is three fit-outs on one 628 x 393 cm shell at 70 mm: Sweden A with shower room at 23 m2 for EUR 13,180, Sweden B with sleeping loft at 23 m2 for EUR 18,000, and this one bedroom version at 22 m2 for EUR 15,500. Buyers who do not need sleeping accommodation should compare Granada (two rooms, 26.64 m2 footprint, EUR 14,730), which avoids the habitation conflict. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the three Sweden fit-outs share a published shell and differ only in internal arrangement and price.

IF ANY OTHER STRUCTURE EXISTS IN THE GARDEN, STEP DOWN A SIZE RATHER THAN GAMBLE: Yardbox's Vancouver and Waltons' Classic 6m x 4m both give a documented 24.00 m2 and leave 6 m2 of the allowance for a shed. THE ONLY OTHER PRODUCT IN THE CATALOGUE AT EXACTLY 30.00 m2 is KC Modular's 6x5m Pavilion, which carries the identical zero-headroom position. IF 30 m2 IS GENUINELY INSUFFICIENT, the honest answer is a planning application — or, for habitable use, the Class 3A route at 32–45 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at the exact limit there is no room for a surveying error, so a smaller documented product is often the better decision.

THE DOMEO 10 IS THE OTHER LASITA OUTDOOR-LIVING MODEL AND CARRIES THE SAME ENVELOPE PROBLEM — 38.25 m2 external against a 19.01 m2 floor — so it solves nothing. WITHIN LASITA, the NEW YORK at 20.40 m2 external is the largest exempt model and the only one listed for workshop and office use. FOR SHELTERED OUTDOOR SPACE AT AN EXEMPT SCALE, Sprout Pod's 3m extended-canopy pod and Dunster House's Dominator Classic Office with Side Canopy address the idea with Irish and UK routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a canopy is lovely and it is counted — size the whole roofed structure, not the room.

Buyers wanting a comparable large single-space room at 70 mm with internally consistent published figures should compare Roland 3 (24 m2, 520 x 520 cm, 27.04 m2 footprint, EUR 16,020, inside the statutory allowance) or Hansa Lounge XXL Pool Edition (24 m2, 783 x 501 cm, EUR 13,780, outside it). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: no published evidence establishes any as the better build; this product is distinguished here only by the fact that its own published figures are mutually inconsistent.

THE DREUX 4 × 4 m IN 44 mm AND 66 mm SHARE THIS EXACT FOOTPRINT AND STATE THEIR WALL CLASS, which makes either a more usable record than this one for a buyer who wants certainty. FOR AN INSULATED ROOM NEARBY IN SIZE, the LILLE 4 × 5 m Insulated at 20 m2 is the range's clearest option. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Loghouse's 4.0 × 4.0 m at 16 m2 and Timber Living's Havana 4m × 4m are direct equivalents with Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at an identical footprint, prefer the record that names its construction.

THE LILLE 4 × 5 m — INSULATED IS THE SAME FOOTPRINT WITH THE SUPPLIER'S EXPLICIT INSULATED DESIGNATION, and for daily year-round use it is the record to work from within this supplier. OUTSIDE IT, Outdoor Living's ModPod Vaya at 18.7 m2 and Loghouse's 4.0 × 5.0 m at 20 m2 are direct equivalents with Irish routes, and MyCabin.ie can be visited in Wicklow, Cork or Wexford. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 20 m2 the market is deep and well documented — there is no need to accept an unspecified wall class.

THE WISSOUS 5 × 3 m IS THE SAME 15 m2 FOOTPRINT IN A DIFFERENT MODEL LINE, and nothing published distinguishes the two on planning or construction. FOR MORE DEPTH AT A SIMILAR AREA, the PREMIUM 4 × 4 m at 16 m2 trades length for a squarer plan. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Loghouse's 4.0 × 4.0 m at 16 m2 and Timber Living's Havana at 4m × 4m are equivalents with Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this area a square plan usually gives a more usable room than a long narrow one.

THE PREMIUM 4 × 5 m AT 20 m2 AND THE DREUX 5 × 5 m AT 25 m2 BRACKET THIS SIZE within the range, and the LILLE 4 × 5 m Insulated is the one record in the range carrying an explicit insulated designation. OUTSIDE IT, Outdoor Living's ModPod Nova at 22.5 m2 and Loghouse's 24.44 m2 unit are close equivalents with Irish delivery and installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the Quick-Garden advantage here is the verified external figure; the Irish suppliers' advantage is a single point of responsibility for delivery, base and assembly.

WITHIN QUICK-GARDEN, THE PREMIUM 6 × 4 m AT 24 m2 GIVES 6 m2 OF MARGIN FOR ONE METRE OF LENGTH — on most plots that is the better trade. The DREUX 5 × 5 m at 25 m2 and PREMIUM 4 × 5 m at 20 m2 sit further inside. OUTSIDE IT, Garden Office Solutions publishes 25 and 26.4 m2 models and Timber Living's Laura reaches 25 m2 at 5.0 × 5.0 m, both in the same band with published figures. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at the top of the allowance, one metre of building is worth more as margin than as floor.

WITHIN QUICK-GARDEN THE NEXT STEP UP IS THE PREMIUM 5 × 3 m AT 15 m2, which is a different order of building. AT THE COMPACT END WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND IRISH ROUTES, Waltons' QCB5 6×8 ft at about 4.46 m2 and QC9 8×10 ft at about 7.43 m2 are direct comparators, Sonic Box serves the small end, and Cabin Master's Micro Office 3.2m × 2.3m is close in size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at four square metres, the internal dimension matters more than the external — ask what the usable width actually is once the walls are counted.

THE SUNNY IS THE ONE TIMBER LIVING MODEL SPECIFIED FOR YEAR-ROUND USE — 93 mm insulated frame, stone wool, vapour barrier — and for a genuine home office it is the honest choice within this supplier. THE NILA AND HAVANA SHARE THIS MODEL'S 45 mm LOG CONSTRUCTION. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Outdoor Living's ModPod Vaya at 18.7 m2 and MyCabin.ie are insulated with Irish delivery and installation, and Sanctum publishes its build-up. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within one supplier, the difference between a log wall and an insulated frame is the difference between a summer room and an office — and only one model here has the frame.

THREE, HEATING IS NOT INCLUDED IN ANY BUILDING — air conditioning at roughly GBP 1,700 plus a two-yearly service, or electric heaters; GBP 9,995 is not a heated building. FOUR, THE ANNEXE GUARANTEE CONDITION: Booths-installed bathrooms and kitchens preserve portability and the guarantee, while THIRD-PARTY INSTALLATIONS REDUCE THE GUARANTEE TO ONE YEAR and prevent the building being moved — and a site visit with quoted groundworks follows any bathroom, kitchen or sink, which weakens the no-concrete-base advantage on exactly those models. AVAILABILITY, DECISIVE FOR THIS ATLAS: free delivery and installation in ENGLAND, a flat GBP 899 to Scotland within 100 miles of Edinburgh or Glasgow, and NO IRISH DELIVERY PUBLISHED — the company is based in Corby, Northamptonshire. Neither applies in Ireland, and an Irish buyer must not rely on the supplier's 'no planning permission' statements. No new outstanding integrity issues arise from this supplier.
